official_source_claims.claim: A Spanner commit deadline can expire even though the transaction may already have committed.
Spanner serializable read-write transactions are atomic and externally consistent, and serializable is the default isolation level.
Cloud KMS CryptoKeyVersion metadata exposes state, algorithm, and protection level, and only enabled versions can be used for cryptographic operations.
Spanner transaction operations can be retried, so side effects outside Spanner can occur more than once.
Cloud KMS EC_SIGN_ED25519 uses PureEdDSA and accepts raw data rather than prehashed input.
Cloud KMS asymmetricSign accepts either data or digest, not both, and supports a CRC32C for data.
Cloud KMS asymmetricSign returns signature CRC32C, checksum verification status, exact version name, and protection level fields that clients can validate.
etcd KV operations provide strict serializability, while serializable read mode can return data stale with respect to quorum.
etcd does not specify operation order for nested transactions, although non-nested transaction operation order is stable.
An etcd client can be uncertain whether an operation completed after timeout or network disruption, and leader election can abort outstanding operations.
etcd snapshot restore creates a new logical cluster with rewritten member and cluster IDs, can move perceived revisions backward, and supports revision bump plus mark-compacted recovery controls.
OpenBao Transit supports Ed25519 signing and verification.
OpenBao Transit signing accepts base64-encoded input and a key_version parameter whose zero default selects the latest version.
OpenBao seal-status API returns the directly queried node's current seal state and cluster identity fields.
In OpenBao high availability mode an unsealed standby can become active after the active node fails or becomes unavailable.
OpenBao Transit rotation creates a new version of a named key while version-specific operation controls remain available.
